records.source_span:
THE LIBRARIAN - ALEX (early 30s, any gender):
They're wearing a Star Trek pin and have a worn copy of 'The Time Machine' on their desk. When the kids nervously ask about local tech history and slip up with future references, Alex notices but doesn't call them out immediately.

Instead: 'You know, I read a lot of science fiction. And either you three are the most creative liars I've ever met, or something genuinely weird is happening. Either way, I'm curious.'

Alex has their own subplot - they wanted to be a writer but took the 'practical' job, and they're watching their dreams slip away. They see something in these kids' desperation that resonates. Teaching them to navigate 1995 technology becomes this beautiful moment of connection across time.

Later, Alex's help becomes crucial - they remember a student who used to come in all the time working on a project, then suddenly stopped showing up. They even remember where the student usually sat, what they were researching. That's the lead that cracks the case.

And maybe in the ending, the kids realize Alex's encouragement helped them, so they leave Alex an anonymous note about not giving up on writing. Small ripple effect.
